utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Judge Chowhan is this morning engaged in other business of the Tribunal. We have decided it's in the interests of justice to continue in his absence. Can I clarify the position about the witness this morning, what is happening?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Our next witness is General Ljubisa Dikovic. We have talked to our colleagues from the Prosecution and from other Defence teams. This general has to travel back to Belgrade already tomorrow, so we will do our very best to finish with his testimony in the course of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Dikovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Cepic on behalf of Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, good morning.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: For the record, please tell me your full name.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Ljubisa Dikovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: 22nd May 1960 in Uzice.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What were the most important positions you occupied during your career?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Several, such as commander of platoon, company commander, battalion commander, brigade commander, Chief of Staff of the corps, deputy chief of operations, deputy commander of the combined command for the operations of the army, and I'm currently --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat, he said it too quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. The very last part of your answer was not picked up by the interpreter. You said: "I am currently ..." Can you give us the post you hold?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am currently acting as commander for training of the General Staff of the Army of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is your current rank?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Major-general, with two stars.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What military schools did you complete so far?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I gratitude from the secondary military school, the military academy, the command staff school, and the General Staff school.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What position did you occupy in 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: In 1999 I was brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Which brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Commander of the 37th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When did the first part of the 37th Motorised Brigade arrive in the area of Kosovo and Metohija in 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: The first part of my brigade arrived in Kosovo and Metohija in the beginning of March 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: On whose orders?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I came there on the orders of my superior command, and at that moment it was the command of the Uzice Corps of the 2nd Army of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What activities was your unit engaged in in Kosovo and Metohija before the war started?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Before the beginning of the war, my unit carried out intensive combat training, focusing on drills in order to increase the level of combat-readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: During the exercises, were you under attack from terrorists?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Just before the war started, did you have an anti-terrorist operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: We carried out our exercise activities in the field, and while performing those regular combat activities we suffered attacks from terrorists, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up in e-court P2039.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, what you see on the screen, is it your combat report -- sorry, is it your operational report, operative report?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I see the last part of this report because I can't see all of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, that is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have again the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please look at the first paragraph marked 5.3.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it describe the activities you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the activities listing the various groups of the Combat Group 37.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: To save time, just look at para 8.4. We see that an operational-- operation is carried out to combat terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we scroll down in English a little bit, 8.4.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that the operation we just referred to, the anti-terrorist one, and did you suffer any losses?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic. 8.4 I can see. I said a moment ago that in the course of performing our regular combat activities there was a totally unprovoked attack by the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were any of your soldiers injured during this anti-terrorist operation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, two soldiers were wounded, as far as I can recall. If you can show me the whole report, maybe it's written somewhere in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the last paragraph on that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English that's on the next page, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You see in Serbian the last paragraph on this page?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two soldiers were wounded by mortar fire, I think, by Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: When did the brigade itself, because until now you've told us about one part of the unit that had arrived in Kosovo and Metohija, when was the brigade itself resubordinated to the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: The exact date when the brigade was resubordinated to the corps I cannot recall now, but I know that in the beginning of April we arrived in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, that is to say the whole brigade arrived in early April.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, to speed up this examination, the document on resubordination is P1473. It's a document from the Supreme Command Staff, P1473. We also have a document of the 3rd Army, that's P1946.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you said earlier, Mr. Dikovic, that you first arrived in Kosovo at the beginning of March, were you referring to a part of the brigade or have we -- have I misunderstood the situation? It was simply a part of the brigade that arrived in March, I think that's in fact what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, part of the brigade arrived in early March in Kosovo, one combat group from my brigade, one combat group from my brigade came in early March; and the whole brigade arrived in early April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. It was my mistake. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By courtesy of Mr. Riaz, we see now on the screen the document from the Supreme Command Staff ordering resubordination, and we also have in e-court a similar document from the 3rd Army, P1946. In order to move more quickly through the documents, can we now have 5D1027.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, do you have it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is a marching order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is it a document of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to see the last page again, just to check. Yes, yes, this is a document of the command of the 37th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you look at para 4: "I hereby decide ..." Third line from the bottom: "Protect the civilian population and prevent the occurrence and strengthening" --

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: "Prevent the emergence and strengthening of terrorist groups."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, that's enough. Was the protection of the civilian population a priority along with defends the country?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I think we can see clearly from this what assignment we received and what assignment we issued to the brigade at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, pursuant to this document, did the 37th Motorised Brigade arrive in early April in the area of Drenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, from this document we can see that it contains in one of its parts the assignment to bring in the troops in the area of Kosovo, that is, marching orders; and in the second part, it deals with the battle order of the brigade and the assignments it is supposed to perform in that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we just look at the heading to see the date. Could you just read the date.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: 1st April 1999, 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me about the area of Drenica where your forces were deployed. What was particular to this area, what was characteristic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: The area of Drenica was the main base, the stronghold of Siptar terrorist forces. You know our history as well as I do, you know that the first -- that the Second World War finished in May 1994 [as interpreted], and in the area of Drenica which is a hornet's nest fighting continued against terrorist gangs until 1947.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, we have an error in transcript, page 8, line 1, I think that witness 1945.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Not 1944? In this area it was 1945, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Dikovic, you've been recorded in English as saying that the Second World War finished in May 1994. Can you correct that for us, please, and give us the date that you did say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's not what I said. The Second World War ended on 9 May 1945, and our national liberation units continued fighting until 1947 with gangs and the vestiges of fascism in the area of Drenica, and that's recorded in history. That's all I said for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] Can we call up in e-court P2030.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, can you see this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Who did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I received this document from the command of the Pristina Corps, and at that time it was my superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From this document can we see the assignment the unit was given?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next document, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But let's go back for a moment. Could you just read out the task, what it says, what the task actually was that the unit was given?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: According to this document you can see that the commander of the Pristina Corps issued the following order: That in coordinated action with the 252nd Armoured Brigade and the forces of the Republic of Serbia, the MUP, that we should carry out vigorous attacks to crush and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces, and if possible secure the main roads and gain combat control of the territory. So I had several tasks, and that is clearly stressed here, to crush and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the area, in the zone, and there were many of them there, and to secure the main roads, main communication lines, and to gain complete combat control of the territory. I'd like to emphasise that this task was received or orders for this task were received on the 2nd of April, and on the 25th of March the state of war was proclaimed. So at this time there was intensive air force aggression by NATO.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we see the second paragraph. It says that there should be combat-readiness to ensure the defence of the assigned zone. Could you tell me were there some echelons of defence; and if so, which echelon were you in?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Cepic, one of the tasks was that the brigade should be prepared to launch a defence in the area in question, because there was the realistic threat and danger from a NATO force aggression on the ground, partly from the territory of Albania and partly from the territory of Macedonia. So what needed to be done was to prepare to defend the zone. Now, within the frameworks of our battle order or combat deployment of the Pristina Corps, we were in the second combat echelon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have on e-court Exhibit 5D384 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did you receive this document sent by the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I think I received this document, and I think you can see that on the basis of the lower right-hand corner. In the square stamp it says that the document was received in the 37th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, would you take a look at paragraph 1, please, and it says there that an officer of the 37th Motorised Brigade was in a passenger vehicle that got stuck in a brook. Did you perhaps -- were you perhaps that officer?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. It wasn't me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: If you want me to explain what this refers to, I'm reading the document now --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, that's not necessary. All I need to know is your answer that you weren't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now next on e-court, please, 5D385 [as interpreted]. [In English] I'm sorry, mistake in transcript, not 3D, 5D385, please. 5D385. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did you receive this order from the Pristina Corps command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the basis of this document, did you later on compile a document of your own?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I think I did. I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well have a look now.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Pristina Corps commander --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 5D1020, please. It is the wrong document. I think that I said 5D1020. That's correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, was this perhaps that order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. May I take a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I think that's the order, and I see here that mention is made of Lozica, that a large group and technical equipment was ..., or rather, were caught grouped in Lozica village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And could we have the second page, count 6, please. I think that in English also is on the second page. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, without having to read paragraph 6, we can see what it says on our screens, but will you tell me what this point means, what does item 6 refer to?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: You mean point 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, energetically prevent all crime, et cetera, what actually does that mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it means what it says, that energetically all crime, looting, and abuse of the civilian population shall be prevented; and if any perpetrators are caught that criminal reports should be filed. I looked at the order as a whole, and I think that the basic sense of this order is to strengthen law and order, to increase discipline generally and the combat capabilities of the unit. Because what happened in Lozica, for instance, was something that could be a target from the air on a small group of people, it's an excellent target, this group of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, we'll now move on to another area. In preparing for my examination, I looked at document -- a document which on e-court is P2031, which I'd like to see, and it says "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija," and it was an order to rout and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces at the 22nd -- I think we have it on our screens now. Anyway, did you receive this order of the 22nd of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I think I received that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now, could you tell me, documents like this, how did you receive them and who did you receive them from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, at this period - and we're talking about the 22nd of March, 1999 - all correspondence and documents of the Pristina Corps were sent by courier service mostly. That is to say a liaison officer would be sent or a courier to take them over, to take over the order and other documents of course, or a liaison officer would come from the Pristina Corps, he would be sent from the Pristina Corps to hand over the documents to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Now, this particular document and similar documents as well with the heading "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, KiM," whose documents were they? What did they represent as far as you were concerned?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it really does seem to say Joint Command for KiM here. Now, I never saw this Joint Command. As far as I'm concerned, to me this represented an assignment, a task, from the command of the Pristina Corps, to whom I was subordinated. I was subordinated to the Pristina Corps. So that's what it says unequivocally, no Joint Command of any kind for Kosovo and Metohija. So when I read this, well this command as far as I'm concerned did not exist, it really did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can -- just -- are you continuing on this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Not really, but something related to that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. Can we see the end of the document, please. Can we have the English final page as well. Thank you. You say that's clearly a document from your commander, unsigned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I'm concerned, this is a document from my commander, but while I'm looking at it now I'm trying to remember the details of it, Your Honour. I think that upon receiving this document I called up the command of the Pristina Corps, General Lazarevic, and asked him -- I said, General, sir, are you issuing this order or is it some sort of Joint Command that's issuing it that I don't know about? And I think that that's the lines our conversation took, and I'm sure the General will remember the conversation. And the answer I was given was that my command was subordinated to the Pristina command and that he was commanding me, he was the command of the Pristina Corps and that he was my commanding officer, because this was new for me, as far as I was concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did he explain to you what the Joint Command was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if you are -- if you're still on this subject, please continue, but I'd like to know when you get to the end of this little section because I want to go back to an earlier exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did anybody from the corps come to see you, any of the officers, and did you talk to them if they did? Did you discuss this order with them?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I think that Colonel Radojko Stefanovic came by at that period and that I discussed this with him, and I think that during that discussion he told me the following: He said that this Joint Command was written up there because of cooperation and coordination with the MUP forces, and I think that was the key to it, why it said "Joint Command" in the first place there. In other words, so that I would know that it was a combined operation with the MUP, and probably in order for members of the MUP to know that it was a combined operation with the army and that the army was cooperating in that action. I think that that was the key to our discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I go back then to an earlier exhibit now. Could we see on the screen, please, 5D1020. Can we go now to the second page, paragraph 6. Yeah. Thank you very much. Please continue, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have Exhibit P2042, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your report?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, second page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is my report sent to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But if we look at item 15 it says: "Pursuant to the decision of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, strictly confidential number 455-54 of the 22nd of March, 1999," why in that document do you say: "Pursuant to a decision of the Joint Command ..."?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I didn't write the document personally. I think that's the main reason, I didn't write this document personally. It was my operations clerk who wrote it and he by inertia, if I can put it that way, he said "pursuant to the decision of the Joint Command." Now, I sent this to the command of the Pristina Corps. I didn't send it to any Joint Command, and let me repeat once again, please, that I -- now, this -- as to the existence of this organization that was commanding, I didn't know about anything like that. The only person in command of me was exclusively and only the command of the Pristina Corps. He was my commanding officer, so I'm sending him the report. I'm not sending it to any sort of Joint Command. So as far as I am concerned, he was my commanding officer and that was the superior unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, during the proofing I showed you document P1968. It's another document bearing the same heading, and it's an order for support to the MUP forces in breaking up and routing the Siptar forces in the Drenica area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screen [Interpretation] 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In item 5 orders are issued, or rather, tasks to the units of the 37th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: 5.1, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you receive this document? Because I see here tasks for your unit.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, could you please show me the document from the beginning to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the first page again. [Interpretation] And can we -- [In English] Can we have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: You see here in item 5, tasks for the units, and a task is assigned to the 37th?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 5.1, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Has this refreshed your memory? Do you remember whether you received this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have Exhibit P2045, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you see the document before you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this a daily combat report sent from your unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's the daily or regular combat report for the 27th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Does it refer to the action carried out pursuant to the previous order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's the action.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please look at item 4. We can see here that the STS opened fire from various kinds of weapons, mostly from the Popova Glava, Izbica, and Kaludjerica, I assume, sectors. Would you tell me if the area mentioned in your combat report was a strong terrorist stronghold?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. This was the area of north-west Drenica, as far as I can recall the features mentioned in item 4. In this area there was a large number of terrorists, and I think that they controlled this entire area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To whom did you address this report?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, please, I did not send any reports to anybody else but the command of the Pristina Corps. So this one also was sent to the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Below that we see to the command of the 2nd Army and UK for information. Can you explain what UK stands for and what "for information" means.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, to the UK command, that's abbreviated for Uzice Corps, and I was resubordinated from the Uzice Corps to the Pristina Corps. So here I'm sending this report for the information of that corps because that was my home unit. So I was resubordinated to the Pristina Corps, but after the resubordination was over I would return to my main or home unit and that was the Uzice Corps. Mr. Cepic, the Uzice Corps was part of the 2nd Army, the 2nd Army of the Army of Yugoslavia, as it was then called.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Let's go back to the opening of fire from that axis. Can you tell us who opened fire from that axis?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was the terrorists who opened fire from that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit IC105, please. Could we have zoom in area which is marked with letter E. A little bit more, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, can you recognise on this map the village of Izbica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic, it says here Izbica between these lines, representing probably some sort of zone or area of the Izbica village. It's in the upper left-hand -- on the upper left-hand edge of this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We heard in this courtroom that this zone marked E -- can you please underline the village of Izbica.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We heard the claim in this courtroom that this zone marked E bordered in orange was a zone under the control of the KLA. Would you tell me whether this entire area was under their control or is your view of events different?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, this was certainly under the control of the Siptar terrorist forces, but I would like to broaden this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you mark where, according to your information and experience, this zone was.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this is the area. Please don't hold it against me if it's not perfectly precise, but that's how I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, on what basis are you saying that this zone was wider, broader, than the one marked on the map?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I think that in my report of the time to the command of the Pristina Corps, it explains it. In the village of Leocina.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you underline it, please?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the village of Leocina, a non-commissioned officer of mine was seriously wounded. He couldn't have been wounded just like that. That was a terrorist stronghold. He was seriously injured. He was wounded. That was the second or third case, and I remember it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have an IC number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC156, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, we saw the previous document, tasks in action; we saw a combat report of yours. Could you please tell me what axis you moved along in that action.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, it's in the task issued by the commander of the Pristina Corps, Vitak, Kladernica, Vocnjak, I think that was the general axis, the general axis of movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you draw a line to mark that axis and where were you overlooking the village of Vocnjak, that's my next question to you, it concerns Vocnjak.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: To the best of my recollection, Mr. Cepic, and please let's take into account the amount of time that has elapsed, so I cannot be a hundred per cent precise, I would like to say that I'm not absolutely sure --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, can you say where Vocnjak was, how far you were, how far away from it you were, and what the axis of movement was?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. On this map I can't find the village of Vocnjak. I don't know whether you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: No, it's not on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we try with 6D228, please. [Interpretation] It seems I'll have to put my question without a map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Cepic, I can tell you approximately where Vocnjak is on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'd like to know. It doesn't have to be absolutely precise, just to give us a general idea, please. We have to use our time rationally. Just mark it with a dot.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that the Vocnjak is about here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you draw a line to indicate your movement?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And where you stopped, draw a circle at the place you stopped.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I spent several days in this area. I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm interested in Vocnjak, overlooking Vocnjak.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was around here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's to the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC157, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have Exhibit P2046, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your combat report?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is. It's a report from my combat group.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you look at the last paragraph, please. "In the forthcoming operations in the area of Vocnjak village we expect several thousand civilian refugees." General, could you please explain to us why you were expecting civilian refugees.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, at that time we were engaged in intensive anti-terrorist activity in this area, the one that was marked here a little while ago and a bit broader than that. Before these actions and before the use of the unit, certain assessments have to be made about the composition and strength of the Siptar forces, their intentions, methods, any possible minefields, obstruction, where they are fortified, and so on and so forth, obstacles. And one has to assess everything the unit might run into during the course of combat, and there was certainly civilians in the area. That's why I was expecting there to be civilians in the area. I was expecting them to turn up. And here, preventively I'm raising the issue and asking for advice as to what to do with the civilians if they turn up in this zone. I don't say here that I'm certain they'll turn up. I'm just expressing the possibility, my assumption, that it's possible civilians might turn up in the zone of combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did terrorist forces have a certain tactic regarding the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I told you about the assessments that I made before combat activities, and of course these assessments include the method of action of terrorists. When carrying out their own activities and actions and making strikes, they often used unarmed population, that is, civilians, as cover. That's where their strongholds were. They kept civilians as a shield, because they probably [as interpreted] knew that my forces would not open fire on civilians. So they used civilians as cover.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We see in this same paragraph towards the bottom, where you are asking instructions and orders how to treat them because you have no resources to block refugee columns and escorting refugees outside the zone of combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, we have an error in transcript. Page 22, line 21, I think that witness said "they knew," not probably knew in relation to terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That will be checked by reviewing the tape, and if it has to be corrected then you'll be notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you are asking for instructions and orders?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you contact anyone from the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I believe at that time one officer was sent from the Pristina Corps to give me those instructions on the spot. I believe one officer was sent from the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you have any further actions on this axis after this document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Maybe movements in the battle order, forward but very little in order to take up a more favourable position vis-a-vis the terrorists. But there were no major shifts, no major movements. I believe I had received instructions, and I needed confirmation from the officer of the Pristina Corps to stop our activities in case civilians appear in our zone. I received an assignment where I should stop, which line I have to reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where in regard to that map? Was the direction the same? Was it changed?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, the direction didn't change. I was moving in the assigned direction towards Vocnjak village.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were you supposed to continue further on from the village of Vocnjak?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: We were supposed to reach the Klina-Pristina road and face the forces there.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you continue moving towards that communication, to the south?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where did you go on from that area?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: From that area I moved towards the area of Srbica; I believe it's in the reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, during this entire operation did you have any contact whatsoever with the civilians?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know what kind of contact you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Any contact whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, if you had known that somewhere a crime had occurred, what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, in case a crime had been committed, I would have acted in accordance with my authority, my powers, and pursuant to the law; that is, if I had learned of a crime having been perpetrated somewhere, I would have ordered a proper investigation, the perpetrators to be arrested and prosecuted, as the law requires, and there's no dilemma there. The procedure is prescribed very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Was anyone arrested for serious crimes in your unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we call up P1969.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Look at the heading, the number, and the date. Did you maybe receive this order as well?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I really need to see the last page again.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have count 5, probably, 5.5, please. [Interpretation] The page before, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see here the assignments given to your units -- to your unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you receive this order?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have P2049, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you look at 5.1, activities; you refer to the order of the command of the Pristina Corps, strictly confidential number 455-90, dated 28th March 1999, the same number we saw on the previous document. Why are you referring to it in this way?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand. I always referred to the orders of the commander of the Pristina Corps, which way?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Well, it was earlier indicated, pursuant to the order of the Joint Command; now we have the order with the same heading but you are referring to the order of the command of the Pristina Corps, not the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, please. For me there was no Joint Command. I was commanded exclusively and only by the commander of the Pristina Corps. Upon learning about this Joint Command, I requested clarification from the commander of the Pristina Corps. We have gone through this, Mr. Cepic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We've heard that already. Let us go back to that area, that zone that you drew on the map, the north-western part of Drenica. To the best of your knowledge, was there any fighting there throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Did I understand you well, Mr. Cepic? You're asking me --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: The area of north-west of Drenica, Izbica, Vocnjak, Leocina village, to the best of your knowledge was there fighting with the terrorists throughout the war there?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: What I know for a fact is that my right-hand neighbour, upon taking control of the zone and my neighbour was the 7th Light Infantry Brigade and they were in that area. During the war they acted in coordination with me and we performed certain actions jointly, and I believe in their own zone they also carried out actions against Siptar terrorist forces, like I did in mine, and I know that we had coordinated action in some operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did you also carry out independent operations during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number P1503, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see an order here from the command of the Pristina Corps. Can you identify it or should we go through the document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: I just need that page where my brigade is.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the fifth or actually the fourth page in B/C/S, please. Count 5.5, please, the previous page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see para 5.1, your brigade is mentioned as having to carry out the assignment. 5.1, please. Are you familiar with this?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, did you perform this action with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, it was planned that we should do it with the 36th Detachment of the PJP, but I believe we didn't carry out this operation together.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you then do it alone, independently?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, independently. The MUP did not take part in this operation for I don't know which reason. They just didn't show up where they were supposed to show up. It's the Prekaze operation I think from this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in e-court we have an order for defence for the 37th Brigade marked 5D1029, but to save time I just want to mark it with a proposal that it be admitted. [In English] Could we have ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter, any objection to that?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Cepic, we shall admit that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Could we have in e-court system Exhibit Number 5D1080, please. Could we have in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it's a document of the 37th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see para 2, third bullet point. You stress here that MUP units had not resubordinated to you yet. I want to ask: Did they resubordinate to you at any time later during the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, MUP units did not resubordinate to my brigade at the beginning of the war, in the middle of the war, or at the end of the war; in other words, in my zone, in my brigade, there was no resubordination of units of the Ministry of the Interior. I stressed that on numerous occasions and I requested assistance in this matter from my superior command, and I indicate here as well that MUP units did not resubordinate to the brigade command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Not under my command, that's what I'm saying. At -- there was just the relationship with MUP forces of cooperation and coordination. No other relationship in my area of resubordination or anything with the MUP forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 5D1062, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Take a look at the heading and the date, please.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this a document compiled towards the end of the war?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: It says the 7th of June, 1999, so yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 9, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Here you urgently ask the MUP in Kosovo to put into effect the plan of engagement in your area, in your zone. So what does this request represent? What were you in fact requesting on the basis of this item, 9?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, a number of times during the war - and I stressed this earlier on - the brigade commander -- as brigade commander I requested and called for the forces of MUP, the Ministry of the Interior, which were located in the area covered by my brigade should be subordinated to me so that I could use those forces and to -- that I could have executive command over those forces in my area of responsibility. Now, that is something I never achieved and that is something that never happened. The area of the 37th Brigade, motorised brigade, was about 900 square kilometres, the surface area of it. It was an area with a lot of space, and it cannot be covered with the troops I had; so I needed more troops in order to establish complete control over such a large area so that there were no spaces and gaps allowing the terrorists to take me by surprise from the rear. And I suffered heavy casualties. Mr. Cepic, during the war in the space of 78 days lost 61 men and over 200 others were wounded. So, Mr. Cepic, we didn't kill ourselves down there; the terrorists killed us, and I had more losses than the Siptar terrorist forces -- from the Siptar terrorist forces double the amount of casualties than I did from the NATO strikes. So I -- and this is the 6th of June here, so I'm asking them again to send MUP forces to control my flanks and the gaps where I did not have any men deployed in order to reduce my casualties and my losses. There were a lot of casualties and a lot of fatalities, and we can see quite clearly here, Mr. Cepic, once again that up until that date, the 6th of June - and now I'm telling you not even later - never were the MUP units subordinated to me. Had they been, I wouldn't have asked MUP forces to be sent in to me on the 6th of June, whereas I suffered heavy losses from all sides, from the air-strikes from the air and from the Siptar terrorist forces. It was hell down there, Mr. Cepic, let me tell you, when you have an enemy encircling you when you have an enemy in the air and an enemy all around you, when you can't deploy your technical equipment, you can't move --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the interpreter have time to translate what you're saying. Please continue but at a more reasonable pace, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. As I was saying, Mr. Cepic, I once again am calling here for these forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We've already heard that but just to save time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm not entirely understanding. You are asking for MUP forces to cover your flanks; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, what I asked for is this: I asked the forces of the Ministry of the Interior to be subordinated to me so that I should be their commanding officer in my own area of responsibility. That's what I was asking for, and here I'm emphasising that I'm going to use them according to the engagement plan, in line with what they were capable of doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I forgot a detail. We saw a report for the 27th and for the 28th here, March, of course, 1999. Could you tell me whether your forces on the 29th of March or the previous days in the area around Cirez village, and perhaps did they enter the village of Kozica on that day, and I'm talking about the 29th of March here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, as far as I remember, on the 29th of March my forces were not in Cirez and in Kozica village. I think in one of the reports it states exactly where my troops were on that date, the 29th of March. So we can take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. There's no need for us to go back to that. Thank you. Now, General, with respect to the problems of resubordination and other problems, did you have direct contacts with General Lazarevic in the second half of May 1999?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, General Lazarevic was my commanding officer. I had daily contact with him, and I always had the possibility whenever the need arose, when I considered it necessary to contact him, I could always do so. I could always reach him so that I really cannot enumerate exactly how many times I was in contact with General Lazarevic during the war, but quite a few times, that is certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to go to Pristina especially because of the problems of resubordination so that you could have a meeting with General Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did go to Pristina, the general would come to my command post too. So as I say, those contacts were mostly either in Pristina or at my command post or in the area of my brigade, and since the corps commander was not linked to Pristina strictly speaking, he toured all the units in Kosovo, he toured my unit too.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as we're on the subject of touring units let me ask you this: Did other commanding officers from the Pristina Corps come to see you, to visit you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and they did so on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could you give us some names who came to visit you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Colonel Novak Paprica, Colonel Radojko Stefanovic, Colonel Momir Stojanovic, Colonel Vicentic and a series of other commanding officers from the Pristina Corps, I can't remember their names now. I can't give you all the names, but there were officers from all levels, from corps commander level to the staff officers in the Pristina Corps command.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Right. Now, did you have visits perhaps from the command of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from the 3rd Army command too in -- at my command post in the area of responsibility of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, General, we were talking about your relationship and ties with MUP, and obviously there was cooperation and collaboration and support, but that there was no resubordination. Now, we saw one action in Prekaze. Did you launch other independent actions without MUP except for this one?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. There were other actions too that we engaged in independently, that my units launched independently in that area in order to rout and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 5D1031, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're now going to move on to another area and discuss check-points, and here we can see a document, it is of the 37th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, is this one of your documents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, I just have item 8 in front of me with my signature and stamp, but yes it is my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, could we have the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can see an order here for establishing check-points, and we can see that -- well, if we look at point 2, paragraph 2, we saw -- see that there were mixed ones together with -- together with the MUP forces and there were independent check-points as well. Now, could you tell me what authorisation the army had over the check-points? What control did they exert?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, each and every unit in an area where it is located - and I'm emphasising this, each and every unit in the area it is found in - had to provide security for itself, had to ensure that its area was secure, the area that it was located in. Now, among other things, other combat operations that were taken to implement that task, one of the elements for providing security for the area is a check-point, to set up a check-point. So check-points were used to secure the area of deployment of that particular unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in other situations, if the check-point wasn't in the area in which the unit was deployed, or rather, were all check-points in the vicinity of deployed units or not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: All check-points which my unit set up and just my unit were within the set area of the unit's deployment. It can't be -- a check-point can't be established within a unit. We wouldn't need a check-point in a unit, so it can't provide security for the unit if it is set up inside; it must be at the approach roads to the unit's area. So in addition to the check-points set up by my own unit there were other joint check-points too, manned by the army and the Ministry of the Interior, for example, but not to provide security for that immediate unit. They had other intentions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What were the intentions at these -- what was the purpose of these jointly manned check-points?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the jointly manned check-points depended on the competence and authority of the army members and the competence and authority of the Ministry of the Interior. The control of movement, the passage of civilians, civilian vehicles, that came under the MUP. So the MUP forces at the check-point would see to that, and then the control of military vehicles, combat vehicles, non-combat vehicles, the passage of soldiers and members of the army, that came under the remit of the army part of the mixed check-point, the mixed check-point manned by the soldiers and the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 5D1032, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did the work of the check-points follow these guide-lines and instructions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, these are -- this is a set of instructions and the check-points functioned according to those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we would like some verification of authenticity of this document. It bears no signature or seal. It's a bit problematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is not an order, it's an instruction. It's just enclosed with the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Let's find out from the witness a bit about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, these instructions, do they have to have a seal and a signature or can they be without those?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Instructions do not have to contain a seal and a signature -- a stamp and a signature because they do not have the force of an order. However, along with this document, these instructions, there is an accompanying order containing a stamp and a signature, which says something like this, Please find enclosed instructions for work at the check-point, and brief guide-lines concerning the application of the instructions. And that document would then bear the stamp and the signature of the commanding officer. The instructions were meant to tell those manning the check-point what to do at every moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Where did such instructions emanate from?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: They emanated from the brigade command. That was the lowest level, brigade level, and then above that would be the corps and higher up. I can't really tell you from which unit these particular instructions came from, but it was brigade, corps, army, General Staff, that was the hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you saying you do not recognise this particular document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do recognise this document. I do, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Tell us what this particular one is. I know it's instructions, I know it's for operating a check-point, but did it relate to a particular order or particular check-points? Did it come from a particular brigade command or what? Tell us more about it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a binding document for procedures to be undertaken by people manning a check-point. They had to comply with this document. This document can only be coming from my brigade or the command of the Pristina Corps. At the moment I cannot tell right now whether it came from the brigade or from the command of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did these instructions vary from order to order or were the instructions standard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were standard instructions for any check-point. All our check-points had these same instructions as to procedures to be followed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, our procedure in relation to exhibits is well-known. The document has been explained by the witness as one he recognises as a standard form that was issued by -- in association with orders establishing check-points. So we will admit this document, but as with all other documents we will assess it in light of all the evidence that bears upon it. We have to have a break at this time, Mr. Dikovic, that will be for half an hour. Could you leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you again at 11.15.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, did you make requests for sanitization of the terrain to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who carried out sanitization?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Sanitization of the battle-field was carried out by units of the civil protection according to the rules of instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 5D1039, please. 5D1039, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this a request for sanitization or clearing the ground?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic. In items 1 and 2 and 3, or rather, throughout the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have some other documents concerning sanitization, so I ask that they all be admitted now PD1035 [as interpreted] an order of the 37th Motorised Brigade dated the 30th of April, 1999, concerning sanitization; further, P, or rather, 5D1051 as evidence of sanitization. [In English] Just one error in transcript, I have to repeat, 5D1035 from 30th of April, 1999, this is the order from 37th Motorised Brigade; then 5D1051; and 5D1060 in relation to cluster bombs and their destroying in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Any problem with any of that, Ms. Carter?

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no objection to 5D1035 or 5D1060; however, 5D151 [sic] I'd like a little more clarification on. It purports to be a record of burial of military persons, but its describing a civilian very clearly so if there's going to be argument made on that later on, I'd like some context of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, you'll need to deal with that one if you're going to continue to seek its admission.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. [In English] Thank you, Your Honour, but I have to speed up right now. Could we have 5D1033.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the effect of that is that 1051 is not admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this an order emanating from your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is an order from my brigade dated the 20th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see here that you state that there were large population movements because of the NATO air-strikes. Will you tell us, please, what were the living conditions at that point in time in that area.

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, the movement of the population was caused not only by NATO air-strikes. It was also caused by acts of terrorism. The terrorists wanted that to happen. They wanted to have as many civilians moving through the area as possible for their own protection. Not infrequently there were terrorists in the groups with weapons concealed under civilian clothing, and then they fired on the units. We have examples of that to this day. Even today you will not see terrorists in uniform carrying out acts of terrorism. Terrorists wear civilian clothes. They strap explosives to their bodies underneath their clothing and they perform acts of evil and we experienced that in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the living conditions were?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: When I arrived in the Glogovac area, I found a very difficult situation. The civilian authorities were not functioning because they were practically non-existent. There were food shortages, not enough, or rather, there was no electricity, there were large numbers of people in Glogovac, large numbers of civilians. There was a threat of infectious diseases, there was no water, and if you observe such a situation you have to do something about it, you have to take steps to improve life for the civilian population in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you tell me, please, we've mentioned NATO air-strikes. There's just one thing I'd like to know: How often was that area targeted? Do you have this information?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. We kept records. Over 700 projectiles were fired in the, or rather, were fired at the brigade area of responsibility from the air at various targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Was a factory hit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the Feronikel factory in Glogovac. It was hit, to the best of my recollection, in early May. And then there was a hunting ammunition factory in Srbica hit in early April during the air-strikes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Were there any civilian casualties in Srbica due to this air-strike?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this factory called Feronikel, what did it manufacture, what was it known for, and what was the danger when a factory of that nature was hit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cepic, I think you know Feronikel is an ore and you know what is made from it. That factory was the main employer for the population of Glogovac. Most of the population had links to that factory, that's where they were employed, that's where most of them earned their living. And I wish to point out that in that factory there was not a single soldier nor was there any military equipment there which might be considered to be a military target.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were there any ecological problems?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. From the moment the factory was hit over the following three days, it was on fire and this was not an ordinary fire. The flames went up as high as a hundred metres. There was black smoke issues from the fire all the time, and that had to have consequences on the -- on the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 5D1034, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my document from April 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We see that here you're asking for humanitarian aid, and in the second paragraph you state that food stocks are running out, that the shops and markets are closed, and what document do you refer to in this document here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just one moment. Ms. Carter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object to the leading form of these questions. I know we're trying to keep short on time, but simply reading out documents to the witness just to confirm yes or no is I think an inappropriate use of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Okay. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, it's not really necessary anyway, Mr. Cepic, once the witness has confirmed that this is his document, then obviously we can read it for ourselves and see what it says. If there's something you want to ask him following on the document, please do so, and you have done so I think, you say that he's referring to another document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So can you deal with that question now, please, Mr. Dikovic, which other document were you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document of mine was addressed to the command of the Pristina Corps, and in the first sentence in paragraph 1, I mentioned that, where it says: "Reference your order, confidential number 28-199/1, dated the 16th of April, and in accordance with item 3 of the said order, we are forwarding a request for humanitarian aid." From what I read, I conclude that item 3 of the corps commander's order told me to secure humanitarian aid. Could I see that document, please, and then I could clarify further.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, that document from the Pristina Corps is in our e-court system with number P1306, but I think that is not necessary right now to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It is already admitted in the system. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, could you tell us the ethnic composition of the population of Glogovac at that time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, at the time this document was written in April when I arrived in the area of Glogovac with some of my units, the population was Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In what percentage?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: 100 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: What about Srbica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Almost 100 per cent. I'm really not aware of exact figures, but almost 100 per cent Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit Number 5D1059, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the top of the document, the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel asked for page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we have the first page, count number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What were you doing in Glogovac, General?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Para 4, the second sentence: "The population in Glogovac ..."

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: We distributed 22 sacks of flour, 50 kilos each, to the population in Glogovac, and this flour we had gathered in the area of responsibility of the brigade, thus we distributed humanitarian aid to the population in that area, and they were really short of food and something had to be done to get food for them because the situation in Glogovac was really very difficult. And just one more thing, I want to stress that we were doing all this at the height of combat activities, before the Siptar terrorist forces were destroyed under air-strikes and 134 of our men were disabled and it was not possible to use vehicles to distribute humanitarian aid and I had to risk the lives of my troops to help the civilian population. That's what I wanted to emphasise.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All these documents of yours that we have seen, do they faithfully reflect the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. It could only have been worse than we described in this paper at that moment, and urgent steps needed to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit 5D1037, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, is this your report on the state of affairs in Glogovac?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, from early May about the situation in Glogovac and there was more than one such report, if I remember well.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: After such reports, did you receive any aid?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The command of the Pristina Corps whom I had contacted had, in cooperation with the civilian authorities and the Red Cross in Pristina, made available a certain amount of humanitarian aid that was distributed to the populace, and I believe that is also covered in our combat reports. In this specific document I ask that representatives of the Red Cross be sent to the Glogovac to assess the situation because that's not my primary job at that moment. I was looking for a specialised organization who would assess the situation and provide basic aid. My primary task was not to provide assistance to the civilian population. There are other agencies in charge of that, but when you see a situation like that, as a human being and a commander of a unit you cannot do nothing, and this correspondence I had with the command of the Pristina Corps is a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have 5D1086, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that 5D1037 was not on the list for documents for this witness, and so we'd just like to bring that to the Court's attention --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. CARTER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry for interrupting. Your Honour, with your leave, I requested 5D1086, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but the reference -- the concern being expressed is in relation to your previous document, which was 1037.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that I requested it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: However, you got lucky, there was no objection taken, and all we're being asked to do is to give you one penalty point.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I have to suffer that. Thank you, Your Honour, I have to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can we scroll up, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- is this your document?

utterances.speaker: LJUBISA DIKOVIC
utterances.text: Can I see the top of the document?
